title: Rollout economics prioritization checklist and calendar — 2026 WIP
content:
Purpose
---
This is a working note for the release engineering + product + infra conversation about how we prioritize rollout lanes based on economics (cost-per-token, tail latency exposure, reserved vs burst capacity), not just feature rollouts. Goal is a compact checklist and 4-week rollout calendar to make decisions predictable and measurable.

Status/context
---
- Branch: release/2026-q4-economics-tuning.
- This doc is intentionally opinionated: it treats cost and latency trade-offs as first-class gating signals for canary progression.
- Intended audience: release-engineering, infra-capacity, product-hosted-api, SRE, solutions-eng.

High-level heuristic (one-liner)
---
Advance a lane only when: observed correctness and latency SLOs are green in canary AND the measured marginal unit-cost delta is within the agreed threshold (<= +12% for experimental quantizations, <= +5% for model swaps). If either fails, hold and run targeted mitigations.

Key definitions (for this doc)
---
- Marginal unit-cost: additional cost per 1k tokens attributable to the change (measured against a 7-day baseline).
- Latency SLO: 95th percentile tail latency for interactive generation under expected qps for the lane.
- Economic guardrail: pre-declared threshold (percent delta) that determines if a rollback, limited rollout, or additional mitigations are required.

Prioritization checklist (decision flow)
---
1) Baseline readiness (pre-canary)
   - [ ] Model artifact and weights validated (checksum, quantization recipe present)
   - [ ] Smoke-run against small synthetic traffic (10k tokens) — results logged to telemetry-run-2314
   - [ ] Capacity booking confirmed: reserved GPUs reserved for canary window
   - [ ] Linked tickets: PRs, infra changes, evals linked in release tracker

2) Canary entry (0-2% traffic) — early safety gates
   - [ ] Functional correctness tests pass (regression prompt set)
   - [ ] Memory / OOM checked under sustained small bursts
   - [ ] Real traffic telemetry sampled to separate streams (control vs variant)
   - [ ] Unit-cost snapshot taken (baseline vs variant) over at least 24h
   - [ ] If marginal unit-cost > +20%: stop. Open action item for cost mitigations.

3) Canary expansion (2-20% traffic) — economics monitoring
   - [ ] 95p latency within SLO for 24h under lane qps
   - [ ] Token-per-second efficiency observed vs baseline (batching effectiveness)
   - [ ] Cache hit-rate (prefix/KV) comparable or better than baseline
   - [ ] Marginal unit-cost within economic guardrail (<= +12% for quantized updates)
   - [ ] If latency regresses but unit-cost improves, evaluate risk tolerance with Product and SRE (document decision)

4) Broad rollout (20-80%) — ramping and fallback
   - [ ] Autoscaler sanity check for sustained throughput
   - [ ] Fallback model variant tested (automatic routing verified)
   - [ ] Cost anomaly alarms enabled (alert thresholds at +8% and +15% marginal cost)
   - [ ] Rollout pause window scheduled if any external event (sales launch, heavy marketing)

5) Full plateau (80-100%) — post-rollout verification
   - [ ] 7-day post-rollout economics report generated
   - [ ] Regression ticket threshold for quality metrics (PSI) set and monitored
   - [ ] If cumulative marginal cost > declared budget impact, schedule optimization retrospective

Escalation and rollback matrix (quick reference)
---
- Severity A (service impact / SLO broken): immediate rollback to last-stable variant + pager duty notify
- Severity B (cost surge > +25% without commensurate latency/quality gain): pause rollout and convene "economics triage" within 2 business hours
- Severity C (minor regressions, localized): slow down expansion; require mitigation ticket before further expansion

Mitigation playbook (common fixes)
---
- Replace quantization recipe with next-best (e.g., int8->int8-mixed) and re-measure cost
- Adjust batching window to trade latency for lower unit-cost (tune per-lane)
- Swap to a cheaper but slightly higher-latency model variant for non-latency-sensitive routes
- Enable prefix caching for high-repeat prompts (deploy caching config change)

Telemetry signals to collect (must be available in preflight)
---
- Per-lane: qps, 95p/99p latency, error-rate, tail-kv-eviction-rate
- Economics: tokens_consumed, gpu_hours, estimated_cost_per_1k_tokens, cache_hit_rate
- Quality: regression_prompt_set_failures, hallucination-alerts (heuristic)
- Observability: sample traces with representative requests (attach spans to release id)

4-week rollout calendar (starter plan)
---
Week 0 (prep) — 2026-10-04 to 2026-10-10
  - Book canary capacity (infra)
  - Finalize quantization recipe + QA smoke runs
  - Create release channel and notify CS / sales if external rollback window needed
  - Owners: Aisha (release owner), Priya (infra), Marcus (SRE)

Week 1 (early canary) — 2026-10-11 to 2026-10-17
  - 0-2% canary for 48h, collect unit-cost snapshot
  - Run regression prompt set each 12h
  - Daily standup: rollback decision if cost > +20% or 95p latency > SLO

Week 2 (controlled expansion) — 2026-10-18 to 2026-10-24
  - Expand to 20% if gates pass
  - Enable economics alerts for +8% and +15%
  - Product sign-off sync on perceived quality delta

Week 3 (ramp to broad) — 2026-10-25 to 2026-10-31
  - Ramp to 60-80% depending on autoscaler health
  - Schedule stabilization window (48h) before final cutover

Week 4 (finalization) — 2026-11-01 to 2026-11-07
  - Finalize full roll and generate 7-day economics/quality report
  - Postmortem/retro scheduled within 5 business days if any mitigation executed

Release notes (draft, for user-facing changelog)
---
Title: Improved latency/cost trade-offs for text-generation route (experimental)
Summary: We are rolling out an updated inference configuration that reduces average cost per generated token for many customers while retaining similar output quality. During initial rollout, you may see brief routing to the prior model if latency or capacity is constrained.
Change log bullets:
- Introduces an alternative quantization profile for large models (saves ~9–12% unit-cost in internal tests)
- Smart fallback routing enabled between standard and low-cost variants
- Observability: new per-route cost metrics visible in Console -> Routes -> Cost
Known issues:
- Rarely, interactive sessions at high concurrency may experience slightly higher tail latencies; automatic fallback is enabled

Open questions / parking lot
---
- What is the explicit budget delta Product will accept for the Q4 release campaign? (PRIORITY: high)
- Do we want a ‘cost-only’ canary lane that limits exposure to infrequent heavy traffic customers? (proposal: yes)
- Should we bake the economics guardrail into the Console rollout flow as a checkbox? (UX/PM)

Action items (next 48h)
---
- Priya: confirm reserved GPU booking and test autoscaler ramp script (JIRA-REL-2314)
- Ethan: finalize telemetry dashboards (cost-per-token + 95p latency) and add alert runbooks
- Marcus: schedule the first canary smoke window and add SRE rotation for Week 1

Notes to self
---
- Keep the language in user-facing release notes conservative. Avoid promising cost reductions across all customers — focus on typical workload impact.
- Capture any manual tuning steps in the infra runbook so the on-call can revert quickly.

End of document (working draft).
